```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(essential8)
```

`score_le8()` accepts raw adult diet intakes with `diet_method = "dash"` or
`"hei2015"`. These methods first calculate the raw diet index, then use a fixed
reference population to assign LE8 diet points. An HEI-2015 total of 80 is not
an 80th percentile or necessarily an LE8 diet score of 80.

The reference cutpoints below are **synthetic teaching examples**, not NHANES
estimates or clinical recommendations. Replace them with validated cutpoints
for your analysis. The AHA advisory specifies NHANES 2015-2018 as the reference;
survey weights, strata, food definitions, and units must be handled when
deriving those cutpoints. Score groups separately when their cutpoints differ.
The package never ranks the submitted patients against one another.

## DASH

The Fung DASH index has eight components. Higher quintiles of fruits,
vegetables, nuts/legumes, whole grains, and low-fat dairy earn more points.
Sodium, red/processed meat, and sweetened beverages are reverse scored.
Each component earns 1-5 points; `dash_total` ranges from 8 to 40.

Supply servings/day for food groups and mg/day for sodium. Fruits include
juice; vegetables exclude potatoes and legumes. Apply the same serving and
food-group definitions to patients and the reference population. The default
input names have a `dash_` prefix so that MEPA's weekly inputs cannot be
accidentally reused.

```{r dash}
dash_patient <- data.frame(
  age = 55,
  dash_fruits = 5,
  dash_vegetables = 5,
  dash_nuts_and_legumes = 5,
  dash_whole_grains = 5,
  dash_low_fat_dairy = 5,
  dash_sodium = 900,
  dash_red_and_processed_meat = 0,
  dash_sweetened_beverages = 0
)

dash_reference <- list(
  fruits = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  vegetables = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  nuts_and_legumes = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  whole_grains = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  low_fat_dairy = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  sodium = c(1000, 2000, 3000, 4000),
  red_and_processed_meat = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  sweetened_beverages = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  total = c(16, 24, 32, 39)
)
```

Each intake vector holds the 20th, 40th, 60th, and 80th percentile boundaries.
An intake equal to a boundary stays in the lower quintile. `total` holds the
25th, 50th, 75th, and 95th percentile boundaries of the reference DASH totals,
calculated using the same intake quintiles. Total-score equality enters the
higher LE8 band. Repeated boundaries are allowed and do not split tied intakes
across quintiles; these are explicit implementation conventions.

```{r score-dash}
# Only the diet component is available in this teaching example, so the
# function warns about unavailable components. We retain only that component.
dash_scores <- suppressWarnings(score_le8(
  dash_patient,
  diet_method = "dash",
  dash_cutpoints = dash_reference,
  min_components = 1
))
dash_scores[c("dash_total", "le8_diet_score", "le8_n_components")]
stopifnot(dash_scores$dash_total == 40, dash_scores$le8_diet_score == 100)
```

## HEI-2015

HEI-2015 uses eight food-group adequacy components, a fatty-acid-ratio
component, and four moderation components. Amounts are converted to densities
per 1,000 kcal, except the fat ratio and percentages of energy from added
sugars and saturated fat. Values between the published endpoints receive
proportional points, capped at the component maximum. The total is 0-100.

Inputs are daily totals, rather than already calculated densities:

- Cup equivalents: total fruits, whole fruits, total vegetables, greens/beans,
  and dairy (including fortified soy beverages).
- Ounce equivalents: whole grains, total protein foods, seafood/plant proteins,
  and refined grains.
- Grams: polyunsaturated, monounsaturated, and saturated fats.
- Milligrams: sodium. Teaspoon equivalents: added sugars.
- Kilocalories: total energy, including alcohol; observed energy must be positive.

Map foods to these groups before scoring, using FPED/FNDDS or another suitable
food database. Include legumes in both vegetable groups and both protein
groups, using each group's appropriate equivalents. Whole fruits exclude
juice; total fruits include juice. Do not enter legumes again after constructing
these component totals. When multiple recalls are used, aggregate all intake
constituents and energy over the same days before scoring; do not average daily
component scores.

```{r hei2015}
hei_patient <- data.frame(
  age = 55,
  hei2015_energy_kcal = 2000,
  hei2015_total_fruits = 1.6,
  hei2015_whole_fruits = 0.8,
  hei2015_total_vegetables = 2.2,
  hei2015_greens_and_beans = 0.4,
  hei2015_whole_grains = 3,
  hei2015_dairy = 2.6,
  hei2015_total_protein_foods = 5,
  hei2015_seafood_and_plant_proteins = 1.6,
  hei2015_polyunsaturated_fat = 30,
  hei2015_monounsaturated_fat = 20,
  hei2015_saturated_fat = 16,
  hei2015_refined_grains = 3.6,
  hei2015_sodium = 2200,
  hei2015_added_sugars = 8
)
hei_reference <- c(40, 60, 80, 95) # Synthetic total-score percentile cutpoints.
hei_scores <- suppressWarnings(score_le8(
  hei_patient,
  diet_method = "hei2015",
  hei2015_cutpoints = hei_reference,
  min_components = 1
))
hei_scores[c("hei2015_total", "le8_diet_score", "le8_n_components")]
stopifnot(hei_scores$hei2015_total == 100, hei_scores$le8_diet_score == 100)

# Audit the 13 individual HEI-2015 component scores.
hei_scores[grep("^hei2015_.*_score$", names(hei_scores))]
```

`hei2015_cutpoints` contains the reference total's 25th, 50th, 75th, and 95th
percentile boundaries. These produce LE8 scores of 0, 25, 50, 80, and 100,
respectively, with equality entering the higher band. The cutpoints are not
the fixed component standards used to calculate the raw HEI-2015 total.

## Column mappings and missing data

Mappings name the canonical field without its diet prefix and specify an
actual data column. For example:

```{r mapping}
names(hei_patient)[names(hei_patient) == "hei2015_energy_kcal"] <- "calories"
mapped <- suppressWarnings(score_le8(
  hei_patient,
  diet_method = "hei2015",
  hei2015_columns = c(energy_kcal = "calories"),
  hei2015_cutpoints = hei_reference,
  min_components = 1
))
stopifnot(mapped$hei2015_total == 100)
```

Input names and mappings are case-insensitive. Explicit mappings must point
to distinct, existing columns. Unmapped fields retain their default names.
Absent or missing diet fields propagate to a missing total and LE8 diet
score. Observed inputs must be numeric, finite, and nonnegative. For HEI-2015,
other available diet component scores remain auditable, but no partial total
is used. `min_components` controls the number of complete **LE8** components
needed for the composite; it does not relax DASH or HEI completeness.

The NCI convention assigns zero fatty-acid points when all three fats are
zero, and ten when saturated fat is zero and unsaturated fat is positive.
Missing fat inputs remain missing. The package rejects zero-energy records
because this workflow scores adult dietary intake with a defined energy density.

The existing `diet_method = "percentile"` pathway remains available for
externally calculated diet percentiles. Do not also supply a non-missing
`diet_value` when using a raw-intake method.

## Sources

- Fung et al. (2008), Table 1 and Methods, "Dietary assessment":
  <https://doi.org/10.1001/archinte.168.7.713>.
- Lloyd-Jones et al. (2022), adult diet metric and reference population:
  <https://doi.org/10.1161/CIR.0000000000001078>.
- Krebs-Smith et al. (2018), HEI-2015 components and scoring standards:
  <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jand.2018.05.021>.
- NCI [HEI standards](https://epi.grants.cancer.gov/hei/developing.html),
  [scoring algorithm](https://epi.grants.cancer.gov/hei/hei-scoring-method.html),
  and [reference SAS macro](https://epi.grants.cancer.gov/hei/sas-code.html).
